lines.text: This is a dieline — the flat layout a carton is cut from. The app reads it, finds the panels, and folds it into the box.
It pulled two hundred and two cut lines and eighteen creases out of the file, and found eighteen panels joined by seventeen hinges.
Red lines are cuts — they bound the panels. Green lines are creases, and every one of those is a hinge the card turns about.
Now watch it close. Every crease turns exactly ninety degrees, and which way each one turns falls straight out of the geometry.
That is a real closed carton. A hundred and fifty four by ninety five by seventeen millimetres, measured off the flat.
The slider scrubs the fold, so you can stop it anywhere and watch how the panels tuck into each other.
Colouring the panels shows all sixteen of them, each swinging about its own hinge line.
It does not need vector input. This is the PNG, traced from pixels by colour, and it folds to exactly the same box.
The artwork on the flat prints onto the box too. Each panel carries the part of the sheet that was printed there.
No box templates and no hard coded panels — just the linework and one folding rule. Thanks for watching.
